text: Which module provides threads in Python?

choices.A: thread_pool
choices.C: tasks

text: What does the GIL guarantee in CPython (up to 3.12)?

choices.A: All threads run Python bytecode truly in parallel
choices.B: Only one process runs at a time
choices.C: Only one thread runs Python bytecode at a time
choices.D: Each thread gets its own interpreter

text: Which socket method blocks until a client connects?

choices.A: accept
choices.C: listen

text: What does recv() return when the peer has closed the connection?

choices.A: None
choices.C: The string "EOF"

text: Which primitive makes N threads wait for each other at one point?

choices.A: Lock
choices.C: RLock

text: Why is wait() on a Condition called inside a while loop?

choices.A: It is faster than an if
choices.B: wait() can only be called in loops
choices.C: The condition may be false again when the thread wakes up

text: What is a race condition?

choices.A: A result that depends on how the threads are scheduled
choices.B: Two threads with the same name
choices.C: A thread that finishes first

text: Which object suits a producer/consumer exchange between processes?

choices.A: threading.Lock
choices.C: A global variable

text: Which socket option lets a server reuse its port right after a restart?

choices.A: SO_KEEPALIVE
choices.C: SO_LINGER

text: Two threads take locks A and B in opposite order. What can happen?

choices.A: Nothing, the GIL prevents any problem
choices.C: The second lock is ignored

text: According to Coulouris, how do the components of a distributed system coordinate their actions?

choices.A: Only by exchanging messages
choices.C: Through one central clock

text: What does "transparency" mean in a distributed system?

choices.A: All the source code is public
choices.C: The distribution of the components is hidden from the user
choices.D: Every node runs the same operating system

text: What is a middleware?

choices.A: A hardware device linking two networks
choices.C: A software layer between the system or network and the distributed application

text: What is the main difference between a parallel and a distributed system?

choices.A: Distributed nodes have their own memory and communicate by messages
choices.B: Parallel systems always use several computers
choices.C: Distributed systems share one common memory
choices.D: A distributed system cannot use threads

text: Which interaction model sends one message to many receivers (1 to N)?

choices.A: Client/server
choices.C: Remote procedure call

text: What happens to a daemon thread when the main program ends?

choices.A: The program waits until it finishes
choices.C: It is stopped abruptly
choices.D: It is paused until the next run

text: What does t.join() do?

choices.A: Waits until thread t has finished
choices.C: Kills thread t

text: Why is `with lock:` safer than lock.acquire() followed by lock.release()?

choices.A: It makes the lock faster
choices.B: The lock is released even if an exception occurs
choices.C: It lets several threads enter together
choices.D: It removes the need for a lock

text: What does an RLock allow that a Lock does not?

choices.A: Several threads can hold it together
choices.B: The same thread can acquire it several times
choices.C: It can be shared between processes

text: What does a Semaphore created with threading.Semaphore(3) allow?

choices.A: Exactly 3 threads, never fewer
choices.B: At most 3 threads in the section at the same time
choices.C: Only 3 acquire calls in total
choices.D: Only the third thread to arrive

text: For which kind of work are Python threads useful despite the GIL?

choices.A: I/O-bound work, such as waiting for the network
choices.B: Heavy computations spread over several cores
choices.C: Only work with no shared data

text: What does cond.wait() do on a Condition?

choices.A: Keeps the lock and sleeps
choices.C: Releases the lock and sleeps until notified
choices.D: Wakes up all the waiting threads

text: What is the difference between notify() and notify_all()?

choices.A: notify is for threads, notify_all is for processes
choices.B: notify wakes one waiting thread, notify_all wakes all of them
choices.C: notify releases the lock, notify_all does not
choices.D: There is none, they are aliases

text: What happens when a thread calls wait() on a threading.Barrier(3)?

choices.A: It blocks for 3 seconds
choices.B: It blocks until 3 threads have called wait()
choices.C: It never blocks
choices.D: It returns at once and counts up to 3

text: What do the threads of one process share?

choices.A: Nothing, each has its own memory
choices.C: Only the standard output

text: Why can `cpt = cpt + 1` give a wrong result with two threads?

choices.A: Python cannot add integers in threads
choices.C: Integers are copied into each thread
choices.D: It is not atomic: the read, the addition and the write can be interleaved

text: What is a critical section?

choices.A: Code that needs exclusive access to a shared resource
choices.C: Code that can never raise an exception
choices.D: Code that runs only in the main thread

text: What is starvation?

choices.A: A thread never gets access to the resource it needs
choices.B: All threads wait for each other in a cycle
choices.C: A thread uses too much memory

text: Why do processes need IPC mechanisms such as Queue or Pipe?

choices.A: They always run on different computers
choices.B: They cannot use the CPU together
choices.C: They share the same GIL

text: What is the purpose of the `if __name__ == '__main__':` guard with multiprocessing?

choices.A: To make the program faster
choices.B: To give a name to the process
choices.C: To stop child processes from creating processes again

text: In which order does a multiprocessing.Queue deliver its items?

choices.A: Last in, first out
choices.C: In random order

text: What must be true for an object sent through a Queue or a Pipe?

choices.A: It must be an integer
choices.B: It must be serializable with pickle
choices.C: It must be shorter than 1 KB
choices.D: It must be created in the main thread

text: What does mp.Pipe() return by default?

choices.A: One queue shared by many processes
choices.B: Two connected ends that can both send and receive
choices.C: A lock and an event

text: For CPU-bound work in Python up to 3.12, which tool is best?

choices.A: threading
choices.B: A single thread with sleep calls
choices.C: multiprocessing

text: Which statement about TCP is true?

choices.A: It sends independent datagrams that may be lost
choices.B: It delivers a reliable, ordered stream of bytes
choices.C: It needs no connection to be established
choices.D: It keeps the boundaries of each send() call

text: Which socket type is used to create a TCP socket?

choices.A: SOCK_DGRAM
choices.C: SOCK_TCP

text: What does accept() return on a TCP server?

choices.A: The data sent by the client
choices.C: A new thread for the client
choices.D: A new socket for the client and its address

text: What does bind() do on a server socket?

choices.A: Starts waiting for connections
choices.C: Attaches the socket to an address and a port

text: Why must send() sometimes be called in a loop?

choices.A: It always sends one byte at a time
choices.C: The data would be received twice
choices.D: It may send fewer bytes than requested

text: Two send() calls of a client can arrive glued together in one recv(). Why?

choices.A: TCP is a stream and does not keep message boundaries
choices.C: The server socket is too slow
choices.D: UDP is used under the hood

text: In a concurrent TCP server, what does the listener do after accept()?

choices.A: Serves the client itself until it leaves
choices.C: Waits for the worker to finish
choices.D: Creates a worker for the client and goes back to accept()

text: What are port numbers below 1024 generally used for?

choices.A: Well-known system services, such as HTTP on port 80
choices.C: UDP traffic only

text: What does `await` do inside an `async def` function?

choices.A: Starts a new process
choices.B: Blocks the whole program until it is done
choices.C: Locks the global interpreter
choices.D: Waits for an operation while letting other work run

text: Why is `await asyncio.sleep(1)` preferred to `time.sleep(1)` in asynchronous code?

choices.A: It sleeps exactly one second, more precisely
choices.B: It runs the pause in another process
choices.C: It does not block the event loop while waiting
choices.D: It is the only one that works on Windows

text: Why does the quiz server never call send() while holding the game lock?

choices.A: send() needs the lock to be released to encode data
choices.C: A slow client would freeze every thread waiting for the lock
choices.D: Sockets cannot be used inside a lock

text: Why is "has someone taken the bonus? if not, take it" done inside the lock?

choices.A: To make the check faster
choices.B: To send the bonus to the logger
choices.C: Otherwise several players could pass the check and all get the bonus
choices.D: Because the bonus is stored in a file

text: Why does the quiz run its logging in a separate process?

choices.A: Because threads cannot write files
choices.B: To keep file work off the game threads and to use IPC with a Queue
choices.C: To get a big speedup from several cores

text: Why does the worker of a disconnected player keep calling the barriers?

choices.A: A Barrier has a fixed number of parties, so the others must not wait forever
choices.B: To keep the player's score in the log file
choices.C: To reconnect the player automatically
choices.D: Because a Barrier cannot be deleted

text: Why is each network message sent as one JSON object per line?

choices.A: TCP has no message boundaries, the newline marks the end of a message
choices.B: UDP needs one line per datagram
choices.C: It makes the messages shorter
choices.D: Python sockets can only send text lines

text: What does the action of a Barrier do in the quiz game?

choices.A: It runs in every thread at the same time
choices.B: It runs after all threads have finished the game
choices.C: It replaces the lock around the scores
choices.D: It runs in one thread before the others are released, to prepare the round
